the_blocking_fact.headline: The one string arrived on 2026-11-17. What still stands between this site and a reviewed application: evidence of the enrolled account, three qualifying sales in 180 days, and the per-link validation the brief itself demands first.
the_blocking_fact.detail: Amazon requires Associates tags to be embedded in the product links on the site declared in the application, and it reviews an application only once at least three qualifying sales have been driven within the first 180 days. This site has zero tagged links, so it has zero qualifying purchases, so the application cannot be reviewed. Meanwhile the three links the whole project was built around are themselves short links carrying no tag, so even the supplied links would not attribute a sale to the owner. Every downstream capability in the brief — conversion tracking, the optimizer, the revenue model, the API enrolment that would let the site publish prices and ratings — sits behind this one missing value. UPDATE 2026-11-17 (session 7264f3c2): the owner supplied the tracking ID shopnow047c-20; every reader-facing product link is now a tagged Special Link emitted by tools/link_builder.py, and the deploy gates fail a product CTA without the tag. The application-review arithmetic is unchanged: no qualifying purchase has been attributed yet, so the three-sales clock has not started. The per-link destination-and-report validation in the enrolled Associates workflow is recorded as pending in docs/product-intent.json, and no conversion figure exists to publish.

what_is_settled: The three supplied links resolve, on four separate dates across four sessions, to the same three listings: a Chefman 6-quart dual basket, an Emeril Lagasse 26-quart French-door oven, and a Chefman 8-quart basket fryer (BR-19, BR-20, BR-21).
The evidence discipline holds at scale: 159 of 159 pages carry the disclosure, no page prints a product price, and every specification row links to the page it was read from.
The machinery is trustworthy: 46 of 46 workflow steps pass locally, and the counts that matter are derived from the tree rather than typed.
The rules are known and quoted: what may be published, what may not, and where the disclosure has to sit.

All five supplied links resolve, re-observed on 2026-11-17 across three independent passes (BR-19, BR-20, BR-21 plus the T59/T60 onboarding records): three air fryers and two kitchen thermometers, which is a category question the owner still owes a decision on (DS-16).
what_is_not_settled: Whether the three listings are the products the brief meant. Nothing in any official document binds a supplied code to a product (BQ-18).
Whether an Associates account exists at all, and if it does, its tag and marketplace (BQ-14, BQ-19).
Which of the 17 published surfaces is the site that would be declared (BQ-15).
Who writes it, under what name, and whether that name is public (BQ-16).
What readers are searching for. There is no demand signal anywhere in the project, so no topic on the topics board can be ranked by expected volume (BQ-20).

decide_first.why: Declaring one site determines what every other change is a change to. It is also the only decision that has to be right before an application names a URL, because an application is not reassessed after a rejection.

Done 2026-11-17: the owner supplied the Associates tag, and it is embedded in every published product Special Link. What remains on this item is smaller and slower: account/marketplace evidence, the per-link Associates-workflow validation, and the first qualifying sales.
It costs under an hour and it is reversible. The T55 rebuild removed the phrase from every reader-facing page; 14 operator and companion pages still carry it.

the_one_thing: If only one thing happens next, it should be the tag. Everything the brief asks the platform to do with real traffic — track it, convert it, optimize against it — is unreachable until a link on a page can be attributed to the owner. UPDATE 2026-11-17 (session 7264f3c2): the tag itself is no longer the blocker - it was supplied, embedded, and gated. The one thing now is the per-link validation in the enrolled Associates workflow and the account evidence behind it; until a first Associates report exists, no conversion figure is published anywhere.
